For a time of forty years the orthodox were in serenity, including in the imperial city , and their communities gathered in freedom of assembly. Then during the days of the fast, John of Sirmin through his cruelty awakened the emperor in a rage against them. He ordered their gathering places to be seized, the altars to be torn out, the priests and their bishops to be apprehended and cast into prison.

From that moment on, as so to speak a vehement storm and tempest with dense dark clouds battering down hail, so did a storm swell up and arise against the calm ship of the holy church of the orthodox , and they were cast into different places of confinement. Some were in prison with murderers , others in praetoria , others in a dekanikon , still others in prison cells under the episcopal palace , others in other places of banishment within the churches . Many fled and were scattered about in all manner of places . What is more grievous is that they ordained the devout bishops once again and demanded that they produce a libellus . Words do not suffice to speak about those things that Christians endured in places of confinement. What is more grievous is that they did not allow anyone the imprisoned bishops knew to come to them or to speak with them at all . Food was given to them, preserving life. They made those who were confined in monasteries - if it is right for them to be called monasteries - endure more tribulations , looking at them with ire, casting the rinsing liquid from their basins at them, giving them instead of wine some vinegar to drink , spoiled wine, or the putrid sediment from foul dregs, so that they could not live.

As for the old man Stephen , a presbyter man who was adorned with divine zeal , when they had confined him, he outright pronounced a curse against them to their face. In their fury, they handed him over to the prefect and he said to the prefect : “Evil wicked one, why do you keep as a Christian alongside those who sent me to you, judging the Christians as a pagan? You are not among the living, unless you immediately set me on fire, a Christian old man, and eat me when I have been roasted.” When the prefect heard these things, he was shaken and sent him to the bishop . That one in a rage sent him into imprisonment in Heraclea in Thrace . He was imprisoned for two years without anyone at all of those who knew him being allowed to be seen by him. As he was not given a garment to change into, he was tormented by lice and grew ill to the point of death. He pronounced a curse so that the synodites would not bury him and so that none of them would offer a prayer for him. God prepared some Romans who were orthodox, and they buried him.

John sent for and had brought a certain bishop, a simple old man, whose name was Paul , and he cast him in fetters. While subjecting him by force, he issued an order that he be reappointed of Antioch in Caria . As though they thought they had defrocked him of the original priestly rank, they reappointed him as if a lay person. Such disgrace even from his own , and they called him “the twice-dipped.” He died from his grief.

For this reason, then cast him in prison and sent the quaestionarii . They beat him with harsh blows until blood gushed forth. After these things, then brought him and tormented him so that he might accept the second ordination. But he shouted and said: “ O bia! I will never accept to be stripped of the priesthood, unless you first also strip me of baptism.” Then there was a great commotion, and Stephen was able to go to the emperor . He cried out: “Christianity has been lost! It has been lost! The ordinances and canons have been corrupted! Look, I have been a bishop for twenty years. But now that I have given myself over to acquiesce to your command, becoming blameworthy, he wants to depose me from the orthodox priesthood and reordain me as one of his own. Let him reveal from which canons he has it! Either he was not aware of and did not know the ecclesiastical canons, or although he knew them, he is disregarding them in his tyranny. Look, he is casting the blame on your majesty. If he at your order is doing these things, then order him to abolish the baptism as well and to baptize again. The nineteenth canon of the 318 fathers, concerning the heresy of Paul of Samosata and those like him, orders them to be rebaptized and then to become priests. Let him reveal from where he came to depose us so that he might reappoint .” The emperor was startled as though from sleep. He despised this deed, ordered that it not come to pass, and immediately made a typos pragmatikos so that no one might venture to abolish the priesthood, except for heresies concerning which the canons give an order.

Then, when John of Sirmin saw that his servant , the persecutor of the orthodox, had perished, he again went to the emperor and began inflaming him even more against the orthodox. But the emperor , in a rage, said to him: “Are the ones whom you are intent on having me persecute pagans?” He said to him: “No.” Then he said to him: “Are they heretics?” He said: “This is not the case, my lord.” The emperor said: “So, you have just testified yourself that they are Christians. How then are you going to persuade me to become a persecutor of Christians as Diocletian and the others? Go sit in your church and be silent! Do not burden us.”
